65: Privacy in brief
66: Read the full Privacy Policy
70: Most of your routine data stays on this phone unless you use an account, a subscription or cloud backup.
74: On this phone by default
76: Without an account, Pebble keeps your routines, reminders, history, proof photos, voice tips and settings on your phone.
80: Cloud backup is optional
82: If you sign in, have Premium and turn on cloud backup, Pebble can back up your routine data, proof photos, sync records and account details to Supabase.
86: Asking before backup
88: Before backup uploads anything, Pebble asks you to confirm that it may include private details you added.
92: No ads or AI training
94: Pebble doesn't sell your personal data, use your routines for advertising, or use your routines, proof photos or voice tips to train AI models.
98: Permissions
100: Pebble only uses the camera, photos, microphone and notifications for proof photos, voice tips and reminders you set up.
111: Terms in brief
112: Read the full Terms of Use
115: Pebble is a routine and checklist app. It is not a medical, emergency, alarm, workplace safety, legal evidence or guaranteed archive service.
119: Accounts
121: Signing out pauses account features on that phone. It doesn't delete cloud data, cancel a subscription or remove anything stored on the phone.
125: Subscriptions
127: App stores handle billing, renewal, cancellation, taxes, payment methods, and refunds under their own terms.
131: Backup limits
133: Cloud backup lowers the risk of losing data, but it is not a permanent archive. Keep separate records of anything important for legal, medical, financial or work reasons.
137: Your content
139: You own what you create in Pebble. Pebble only processes it as needed to provide, secure, support, maintain, debug, and operate the app.
143: Fair use
145: Do not bypass subscription checks, upload harmful content, misuse the service, or upload content you do not have the right to use.
156: Deleting your account
158: You can delete your Pebble account from Your account. If you can't get into the app, contact support.
162: What cloud deletion covers
164: Pebble will delete or irreversibly de-identify cloud account data and cloud backup data associated with the account, except where limited retention is required.
168: Deletion timing
170: Active cloud account data is normally deleted within 30 days. Backup copies may remain for up to 90 days before expiry.
174: Local data may remain
176: Deleting your account doesn't always remove routines, history, proof photos, voice tips or settings already stored on your phone.
180: Subscriptions are separate
182: Deleting your account, uninstalling Pebble or signing out doesn't cancel an app store subscription. Cancel it in your app store's subscription settings.
334: Owner and contact

### web/delete-account.html
[content] width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0
Delete Your Account | Pebble Routines
Account deletion
How to delete your Pebble account
How to delete your Pebble Routines account, and what happens to your account, your cloud backup, the data on your phone and your app store subscription.
Contact:
support@pebbleroutines.com
support@pebbleroutines.com
Delete your account in the app
If you can still open Pebble, the quickest way is to delete your account in the app:
Open
Your account
in Pebble.
Scroll to the account section.
Tap
Delete account
Confirm the deletion request.
Delete your account without the app
If you cannot access Pebble, you can request deletion with this form or by emailing
support@pebbleroutines.com
Email address linked to your Pebble account
Optional message
[placeholder] Anything that helps us identify the account
I understand this requests deletion of cloud account data and cloud backup data associated with this Pebble account.
Submit deletion request
To help us process the request safely, send the request from the email address associated with your Pebble account if possible, and include:
the subject line
Pebble account deletion request
the email address linked to the account
any details that help us identify the account
Email link:
support@pebbleroutines.com
What we delete
When your Pebble account is deleted, we will delete or irreversibly de-identify the cloud account data and cloud backup data associated with that account, except where limited retention is required for legal, security, fraud-prevention, tax, accounting, dispute, or backup-retention reasons.
Proof-photo backup only keeps photos for a short, rolling period. Premium cloud copies of proof photos are normally kept for up to 21 days, unless you delete them earlier.
Active cloud account data is normally deleted within 30 days. Backup copies may remain for up to 90 days before automatic expiry, unless longer retention is required by law, security, fraud prevention, accounting, or dispute handling.
What may remain on your device
Pebble is local-first. Deleting your account does not necessarily remove routines, history, proof photos, guidance audio, drafts, settings, or other app data already saved locally on your device. You may need to delete that data manually, clear app data, or uninstall the app if you want local device data removed as well.
Pebble only deletes its own private app copies. It does not delete photos from your camera roll or photo library.
Subscription cancellation
Deleting your Pebble account, uninstalling the app, or signing out does not automatically cancel a subscription billed through an app store. To stop future renewals, you must cancel through the relevant app-store subscription settings.
Questions
If you need help with deletion or privacy requests, contact
privacy@pebbleroutines.com
or
support@pebbleroutines.com
Also see
Privacy Policy
and
Terms and Conditions

### web/privacy.html
[content] width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0
[content] Privacy Policy for Pebble Routines, a local-first routine support app with optional account, subscription, backup, and completion email features.
Privacy Policy | Pebble Routines
[aria-label] Pebble Routines home
P
Pebble Routines
Menu
[aria-label] Primary navigation
Home
Privacy
Terms
Support
Privacy Policy
What Pebble collects, and why
Pebble Routines is a routine app that keeps your data on your phone by default. Most routine content stays there unless you choose to use an account or cloud backup.
Last updated:
3 October 2026
Contact:
privacy@pebbleroutines.com
Short version
Pebble does not sell your personal data, show ads, use your routines or proof photos for ads, or use your private routine content to train AI models. There is no ad SDK and no behavioural analytics SDK in the app.
[aria-label] Table of contents
On this page
Local-first use
Accounts and backup
Subscriptions
Completion emails
Crash reports
Sensitive content
Permissions
Why we use data
Providers
International transfers
Retention
Children
Your rights
Changes
Contact
Local-first use
You can use Pebble without an account. In local-only use, Pebble stores routine titles, steps, reminders, settings, history, optional proof photos, and guidance-audio recordings on your device.
Reminders are scheduled by your device's operating system. Pebble does not use a push-notification server. On Android, the home-screen widget shows routine details that Pebble saves on your device for the widget.
Free local history and Pebble-owned proof-photo copies are kept for a short recent-history window. Pebble only removes its own private app copies; it does not delete photos from your camera roll or photo library.
Local data may be lost if you delete the app, clear app data, lose your device, change devices before backup completes, or your device storage fails. Pebble is routine support, not permanent archive storage.
Accounts and backup
Signing in is optional. You can sign in with an email one-time code, Google, or Apple where available. If you sign in, Pebble processes your email address, account ID, sign-in provider, authentication session, and sign-in times.
Pebble asks Google and Apple for your email address only. Google may still include your name and profile picture link in the sign-in details it returns, and our sign-in provider may store them with your account record. Pebble does not use or show them. Apple may give us a private relay email address instead of your real one.
Like most online services, our sign-in and database provider records technical details such as IP address and device or browser information when your app connects, for security and abuse prevention.
Premium cloud backup requires an active paid subscription, sign-in, and your explicit choice to turn backup on. If enabled, Pebble may back up supported routine data, including routines, reminders, recent history, proof-photo files, and proof-photo records. Guidance audio files currently stay on your device, though routine backup may include related details such as filename, duration, MIME type, or byte size.
Before cloud backup uploads supported routine data, Pebble asks you to confirm that backup may include sensitive user-added content. We keep a record of that choice, including when you made it and the app, privacy, and terms versions shown at the time.
Subscriptions
Personal Premium is sold as a monthly or yearly subscription through Google Play or the App Store. The store handles payment. Pebble never receives your card or bank details.
We use RevenueCat to check subscription status and restore purchases. RevenueCat receives an app user ID (a random ID before you sign in, then your Pebble account ID), your purchase history for Pebble (product, purchase and renewal dates, status, and store transaction details), and basic device and app information such as platform, operating system version, and app version.
Pebble also keeps a subscription record with your account: the product, store, status, subscription period, and a one-way hash of the store purchase token. This is used to unlock Premium cloud features and to stop one purchase being claimed by several accounts.
Completion emails
Signed-in Premium users can choose one email contact for a routine. Pebble first emails that person an invitation. Pebble only sends completion emails after they accept, and every email includes links to stop the emails or block the sender.
The invitation and every completion email show the sender's account email address, so the person knows who they are from. A completion email can include the routine name, completion time, and step count. The sender can hide the routine name. Photos and checklist details are not included.
To do this, Pebble stores the contact's email address, invitation status, and email preferences, plus a log of emails sent (completion time, step counts, delivery status, and the routine name only if it was shown). Emails are delivered by Resend.
If a contact declines or stops the emails, the sender cannot invite them again for 30 days. If a contact blocks the sender, Pebble keeps their email address and a hashed copy linked to the sender's account so the sender cannot invite them again. A contact can also block invitations from everyone using Pebble; for this Pebble keeps only a hashed copy of their address, not linked to any account.
Only add someone who knows you and expects these emails. If you received a Pebble email you did not expect, you can block it from the email or contact
privacy@pebbleroutines.com
Crash reports
Release builds may use Sentry to receive crash reports, so we can find and fix problems. A crash report contains technical details: the error and stack trace, device model, operating system version, app version and build, and a short trail of recent technical app events.
That trail can include internal technical identifiers.
Crash reporting is set up so it does not send your name, email address, routine content, photos, or audio. Pebble removes user details from app crash reports before they are sent, and does not use screenshots, session replay, or performance tracing.
Sensitive content you choose to add
Pebble does not ask for medical records or clinical labels. The routines, notes, reminders, photos, audio, and history you choose to create may still reveal private details about your home, family, workplace, habits, health, or personal circumstances.
Please avoid capturing other people, children, private documents, addresses, financial information, or sensitive third-party details in proof photos unless you have permission and a good reason.
Device permissions
Camera
is used when you choose to capture a proof photo.
Photos or media library
is used when you choose an existing proof photo, or save a copy to Photos. Pebble does not scan your library.
Microphone
is used when you choose to record short guidance audio.
Notifications
are used for routine reminders you set.
Pebble does not request location, contacts, SMS, or phone permissions.
Why we use data
Where UK or EU data protection law applies, we rely on these legal bases:
Contract:
to provide sign-in, Premium, backup, restore, account deletion, and the features you ask for.
Consent:
for cloud backup of content you add (which may include health or other sensitive details) and for completion emails. You can withdraw consent at any time.
Legitimate interests:
to keep Pebble secure, fix crashes, prevent purchase misuse, and stop unwanted invitation emails.
Legal obligation:
to keep records we must keep for tax, accounting, or legal reasons.
Service providers
We use providers only where needed to run Pebble. Supabase, RevenueCat, Sentry, and Resend process data on our behalf under their data processing terms. Google and Apple handle sign-in and payments under their own privacy policies.
Supabase
for sign-in, database, private photo storage, server functions, and account deletion requests. Pebble's Supabase project is hosted in the USA.
RevenueCat
(USA) for subscription status, purchase restore, and purchase history.
Google
for Google sign-in and Google Play billing.
Apple
for Sign in with Apple and App Store billing where available.
Sentry
(USA) for crash reports, in builds where crash reporting is turned on.
Resend
(USA) for delivering completion emails and their invitations.
Email and support tools
when you contact us, and the email service that sends sign-in codes.
App stores and operating systems may also provide their own store analytics, payment records, or diagnostics under their own privacy policies.
International transfers
Pebble is run from the United Kingdom. If you sign in, back up, subscribe, send completion emails, or a crash report is sent, your data is processed in the USA by the providers listed above.
Where UK or EU law requires it, we rely on safeguards such as the UK International Data Transfer Addendum or Standard Contractual Clauses in our providers' data processing terms, or the UK Extension to the EU-US Data Privacy Framework where a provider is certified. Contact us for more detail.
Retention
We keep data only as long as needed for the app, support, security, fraud prevention, accounting, legal, dispute, or backup reasons.
Data or feature
Typical retention
Free local history and Pebble-owned proof-photo copies
48 hours, unless deleted earlier
Premium recent history in the app and cloud proof-photo copies
Rolling 21-day window, unless deleted earlier
Backed-up routines, reminders, and text history records in your cloud account
Until you delete them or delete your account
Completion email contacts and blocks
While your account exists; deleted with your account. Removed or declined contacts are deleted after 90 days. Opt-outs from all Pebble invitations are kept as a hashed address so they keep working
Sent completion email log
90 days. Invitation links expire after 14 days; links in completion emails after 90 days
Subscription and purchase-check records
While your account exists, then as needed for accounting and fraud prevention. RevenueCat and the app stores keep their own records
Crash reports
Up to 90 days in Sentry
Web account deletion requests
As long as needed to complete the request and show it was handled
Account deletion
Active cloud account data normally deleted within 30 days; backup copies may remain up to 90 days
Children
Pebble is not designed for children and is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly create accounts for children under 13. If you think a child has given us personal data, contact us and we will delete it.
Your rights
Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to, or receive a copy of your personal data. You may also withdraw cloud-backup consent by pausing cloud backup in the app, deleting your account, or contacting us.
You can request account deletion through the
account deletion page
. The web form collects the email address you enter, your optional message, a hashed form of your IP address, and your browser's user agent, so we can find the account and prevent abuse.
If you are in the UK, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at
ico.org.uk
. In the EU, you can contact your local data protection authority. We would like the chance to help first, so please contact us.
Changes to this policy
If we change how Pebble uses personal data, we will update this page and the date at the top. If a change is significant, we will also tell you in the app before it applies.
Owner and contact
Pebble Routines is currently run by an independent developer in Scotland, United Kingdom. For legal and data-protection purposes, the controller is Jamie Bray trading as Pebble.
Privacy:
privacy@pebbleroutines.com
Support:
support@pebbleroutines.com
Pebble Routines.

### web/terms.html
[content] width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0
[content] Terms for Pebble Routines, a routine support app for everyday checks, reminders, optional proof photos, and private-by-default records.
Terms | Pebble Routines
[aria-label] Pebble Routines home
P
Pebble Routines
Menu
[aria-label] Primary navigation
Home
Privacy
Terms
Support
Terms
The rules for using Pebble
These terms explain the ground rules for Pebble Routines. Pebble is a routine support app, not a medical, emergency, workplace safety, legal evidence, or guaranteed archive service.
Last updated:
3 October 2026
Contact:
support@pebbleroutines.com
[aria-label] Table of contents
On this page
Agreement
What Pebble does
Accounts
Subscriptions
Backup limits
Your content
Fair use
Availability
Legal limits
Contact
Agreement
By downloading, accessing, or using Pebble, you agree to these Terms and the
Privacy Policy
. If you do not agree, please do not use Pebble.
What Pebble does
Pebble helps you create, run, and remember routines. Depending on the version and plan, features may include routine creation, reminders, history, proof photos, guidance audio, themes, account sign-in, subscriptions, backup, restore, and sync.
Pebble is meant for routine support and personal record-keeping. It should not be used as your only record for anything legally, medically, financially, operationally, or otherwise critical.
Accounts
Pebble can be used without an account for local-only use. If you sign in, keep your sign-in method secure and tell us if you think your account has been compromised.
Signing out pauses account-linked features on that device. It does not delete cloud data, cancel subscriptions, or remove local data already stored on your device.
Subscriptions and billing
Pebble works free. Personal Premium is an optional monthly or yearly subscription bought through Google Play or the App Store. App stores handle billing, renewal, cancellation, taxes, payment methods, and refunds under their own terms. Pebble uses RevenueCat to check subscription status.
Subscriptions renew automatically until you cancel in the store's subscription settings. When you cancel, Premium normally stays on until the end of the period you paid for.
When Premium ends, new cloud uploads stop. Longer history and extra routines stay available for a 7-day grace period, counted from when Pebble confirms with the store that Premium has ended. After that, free limits apply: history older than 48 hours is removed from the device, and routines beyond the free limit are locked but not deleted (you choose which ones stay unlocked). Renewing Premium unlocks them again.
Deleting your Pebble account, uninstalling the app, or signing out does not cancel an app-store subscription. To stop future renewals, cancel through the relevant app-store subscription settings.
Backup and data-loss limits
Pebble is local-first. Local data may be lost if you delete the app, clear app data, lose your device, change devices before backup completes, disable permissions, use unsupported operating system settings, or experience device or storage failure.
Paid cloud backup can reduce some risk, but it is not guaranteed permanent storage. Sync can fail or be delayed because of connectivity, permissions, battery restrictions, subscription status, provider outages, account problems, storage limits, user deletion, or software errors.
Free recent history and Pebble-owned proof-photo copies are kept for 48 hours. Premium recent history and cloud proof-photo copies are kept in a rolling 21-day window, unless deleted earlier.
Your content
You own the routines, photos, audio, notes, and other content you create in Pebble. You give Pebble a limited licence to host, copy, transmit, store, back up, display, and process that content only as needed to provide, secure, support, maintain, debug, and operate Pebble.
Pebble does not use your routines, proof photos, guidance audio, or sensitive user-added content to train AI models or for advertising.
Fair use
You agree not to:
use Pebble for unlawful, abusive, fraudulent, or harmful purposes
try to bypass subscription checks, security controls, or technical limits
upload malware or content intended to damage devices or systems
probe, interfere with, reverse engineer, or disrupt Pebble or its providers
misrepresent your identity, authority, or relationship with another person
add someone as a completion email contact unless they know you and expect those emails
Availability and changes
Pebble may change over time. Features, fair-use limits, storage limits, upload limits, supported file types, retention rules, or access rules may be updated.
Cloud backup means short-term backup for supported plan data. It does not mean permanent archive storage, legal evidence storage, workplace compliance storage, or an emergency safety system.
Legal limits
Pebble is provided on an "as is" and "as available" basis to the fullest extent permitted by law. Nothing in these Terms excludes or restricts statutory rights that cannot be excluded or restricted by law.
These Terms are governed by the laws of Scotland, except where mandatory consumer law provides otherwise.

, so the time * is shown in the sender's zone with the offset spelled out. * - Older builds sent a local wall-clock time with no zone. The edge runtime * runs in UTC, so formatting in UTC shows that wall-clock time unchanged. * - A zoned timestamp with no offset is shown in UTC and labelled. */ export function formatCompletionTime(input: { completedAt: Date; utcOffsetMinutes: number | null; completedAtHasZone: boolean; }): string { const shifted = input.utcOffsetMinutes === null ? input.completedAt : new Date(input.completedAt.getTime() + input.utcOffsetMinutes * 60 * 1000); const text = shifted.toLocaleString('en-GB', { timeZone: 'UTC', day: 'numeric', month: 'short', year: 'numeric', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', hour12: false, }); if (input.utcOffsetMinutes !== null) return

; } export function formatDate(date: Date): string { return date.toLocaleDateString('en-GB', { timeZone: 'UTC', day: 'numeric', month: 'long', year: 'numeric', }); } // --------------------------------------------------------------------------- // Abuse limits // --------------------------------------------------------------------------- export type InviteCounts = { suppressed: boolean; blocked: boolean; senderInvitesLastDay: number; senderRecipientInvitesLastWeek: number; recipientInvitesLastDay: number; /** Pending or accepted contacts on the sender's other routines. */ activeContactsElsewhere: number; /** Set while a recent decline stops this sender re-inviting the address. */ declinedUntil: Date | null; }; export type Refusal = { ok: false; status: number; code: string; error: string }; export function inviteDecision(counts: InviteCounts, now: number): { ok: true } | Refusal { if (counts.suppressed) { return refuse(403, 'recipientOptedOut', 'This email address does not accept Pebble invitations.'); } if (counts.blocked) { return refuse(403, 'recipientBlocked', 'This recipient has blocked invites from this account'); } if (counts.declinedUntil && counts.declinedUntil.getTime() > now) { return refuse( 409, 'recentlyDeclined',

## Store copy (docs/store/)

### docs/store/GOOGLE_PLAY_LISTING.md
# Google Play Store Listing: Pebble Routines
Last updated: 4 October 2026
Ready-to-paste copy for Play Console > Grow > Store presence > Main store
listing, plus the policy questionnaires. Every limited field is in a fenced
block with a `limit` marker. Run `python3 docs/store/check_limits.py` after
any edit. The latest counts are in the table at the end.
Copy rules applied (from `COPY_GUIDELINES.md` and `COPY_RISK_SCAN.md`):
- Plain, direct, UK spelling. No "worry less", "peace of mind" promises,
  "never worry again", "stay safe", "evidence", "guaranteed backup".
- No medical claims. "OCD" and "anxiety" are deliberately left out of the
  listing. Using them would present Pebble as a health product, invite Play
  health-claim review, and risk reading as a promise to people who are
  struggling. The audience still finds Pebble through the words they actually
  type: "did I lock the door", "leaving the house checklist", "hair
  straighteners", "stove off".
- Backup always comes with "if you have Premium, sign in, and turn it on".
- "Photo" in daily copy. "Proof photos" only as a feature name.
Search terms used: did I lock the door, checklist, leaving the house, leaving
home, hair straighteners, straighteners, curling iron, stove, oven, unplug,
front door, locked, routine, reminder, photo, bedtime check, hotel checkout,
car lock, trip.
About "peace of mind": the brief lists it as a search term, but
`COPY_GUIDELINES.md` lists "Unlock peace of mind" as copy to avoid. It is left
out of the copy below. If you want it indexed, the only wording I would use is
the neutral optional line at the end of the full description section. It
describes what people say, not what Pebble promises.
---
## App name (max 30)
Recommended:
<!-- limit:30 id:play-name -->
```text
Pebble Routines: Checklist
```
Alternatives, if you would rather put the top search phrase in the title.
Google Play allows descriptive phrases in titles. It does not allow "free",
"best", "#1", emoji or all caps.
<!-- limit:30 id:play-name-alt-1 -->
```text
Pebble: Leaving Home Checklist
```
<!-- limit:30 id:play-name-alt-2 -->
```text
Pebble: Did I Lock The Door?
```
Note: the launcher label in `AndroidManifest.xml` is "Pebble Routines". A Play
title that is different from the launcher label is allowed.
## Short description (max 80)
Recommended:
<!-- limit:80 id:play-short -->
```text
Did I lock the door? Run your leaving-home checks step by step and add a photo.
```
Alternatives:
<!-- limit:80 id:play-short-alt-1 -->
```text
A step-by-step checklist for the door, the stove and the hair straighteners.
```
<!-- limit:80 id:play-short-alt-2 -->
```text
Check the door, stove and straighteners, with a photo and the time saved.
```
## Full description (max 4000)
<!-- limit:4000 id:play-full -->
```text
Did I lock the door? Did I unplug the hair straighteners? Is the stove off?
Pebble Routines turns the checks you do before leaving the house into a step-by-step checklist. Go through each step, mark it done, and add a photo when you want something to look back on later. Every completed check is saved with the time you did it.
Pebble is for anyone who has turned back at the front door to check it again, or taken a photo of the straighteners just in case.
HOW IT WORKS
• Create a routine. For example "Leaving the house": straighteners or curling iron unplugged, stove and oven off, windows shut, back door locked, front door locked.
• Run it step by step. One clear screen per step, so the next check is always obvious.
• Add a photo on any step. Take it in the moment, or choose one you already have.
• Look back. Recent history shows what you checked and when.
READY-MADE ROUTINES YOU CAN EDIT
• Everyday departure check: hair tools, stove and oven, toaster, sink, heaters, windows and doors
• Bedtime house check
• Car lock and parking check
• Hotel checkout sweep
• Big trip home shutdown
• School morning run, gym bag, morning pet routine, office switch-off and more
USEFUL EXTRAS
• Reminders: a notification at the time you usually leave
• Home-screen widget: start a routine with one tap
• Voice prompts: record a short note in your own voice for any step (Premium)
• Save a copy to Photos: keep a photo from Pebble in your own gallery
• Themes, including accessibility themes
PRIVATE BY DEFAULT
• Works without an account. No sign-up needed to start.
• Your routines, history and photos are stored on this device.
• No ads. Pebble does not sell your data.
• On the free plan, photos and history are kept for 48 hours, then Pebble deletes its own copies. Pebble never deletes anything from your camera roll.
• Cloud backup only starts if you have Premium, sign in, and choose to turn it on.
FREE
• 2 routines, up to 10 steps each
• 1 photo per step
• 48 hours of recent history
• Reminders, ready-made routines and the home-screen widget
PERSONAL PREMIUM (MONTHLY OR YEARLY)
• Unlimited routines and steps
• Up to 4 photos per step
• 21 days of recent history
• Voice prompts on any step
• Extra themes
• Optional cloud backup and account recovery (needs sign-in and your consent)
• Completion emails: Pebble can email one contact when a routine is done. They accept first, and can stop the emails at any time. Photos and checklist details are not included.
Premium renews automatically until you cancel in Google Play. Pebble keeps working on the free plan without it.
WHAT PEBBLE IS, AND IS NOT
Pebble is a routine and checklist app. It is not a medical app or treatment, a home security system, or an emergency service, and photos in Pebble are not legal evidence. If checking is taking up a lot of your day, a doctor or other qualified professional can help.
Privacy policy: https://pebbleroutines.com/privacy
Support: support@pebbleroutines.com
```
Optional neutral line, only if you decide you want "peace of mind" indexed. Put
it after the paragraph that starts "Pebble is for anyone who...":
```text
Some people call it peace of mind. Pebble calls it a checklist with the time on it.
```
Check the length again after adding it.
## Category and tags
- **App category:** Productivity
- **Secondary option if you want to test it later:** Lifestyle. Productivity
  is the closer match for "checklist" and "routine" searches, and the
  competitors there are general to-do apps rather than health apps.
- **Tags (Play Console > Store settings > Manage tags, up to 5):** pick the
  closest available entries from Google's list. Suggested order:
  1. To-do list / Checklist
  2. Reminders
  3. Planner
  4. Habit tracker (only if no closer "routine" tag is offered)
  5. Personal organiser / Productivity tools
  Do not pick health, wellness, or mental health tags.
- **Contact details:** email `support@pebbleroutines.com` (confirm the domain;
  see `OWNER_NOTES.md`), website `https://pebbleroutines.com`, privacy policy
  `https://pebbleroutines.com/privacy`.

| Does the app let users interact or exchange content with other users? | **Yes** | Conservative answer. Completion emails send text the user typed (the routine name) to one email contact who has accepted. It is one-way, opt-in, and has stop and block links. There is no chat, profile, public feed, or in-app messaging. If you want to answer No, the argument is that this is a system notification, not user-to-user messaging. Yes only adds a "Users Interact" note and does not change the age rating. |

## Target audience and content

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Target age groups | **18 and over** only |
| Could the app unintentionally appeal to children? | No. No cartoon characters, games, or child-directed content. The store listing and screenshots are adult and practical. |
| Store listing shown to children? | Not applicable |
Why 18+ only: choosing any group under 13 brings in the Families policy, and
choosing 13 to 17 adds extra checks on content and ads. The school-run and
toddler-bag templates are for parents, not for children. Teenagers can still
install the app; this answer only sets who it is designed for. The privacy
policy states Pebble is not directed at children under 13.

## Feature graphic concept (1024 x 500)
- **Background:** Pebble forest green `#2C4434` (the adaptive icon
  background), with a soft lighter band behind the phone.
- **Left half:** the cairn icon and "Pebble Routines" in the site serif, with
  one line below: "Leaving-home checks, step by step".
- **Right half:** a cropped phone showing three check cards, matching the
  website hero: "Straighteners unplugged, 08:02" with a small photo
  thumbnail, "Stove off, 08:02", "Front door locked" as the active step.
- **No** price, ratings, "free", award badges, or small text. Google crops
  and overlays the graphic, so keep important content away from the edges.
- **Accessibility:** white text on the green passes contrast. Do not put
  text over the photo thumbnail.

### docs/store/APP_STORE_LISTING.md
# App Store Listing: Pebble Routines (iOS)
Last updated: 4 October 2026
Ready-to-paste copy for App Store Connect. Limited fields are in fenced blocks
with a `limit` marker; run `python3 docs/store/check_limits.py` after any edit.
The same copy rules as `GOOGLE_PLAY_LISTING.md` apply: no medical claims, no
"OCD" or "anxiety", no "peace of mind" promise, and backup always comes with
"Premium, sign in, and turn it on".
> **iOS status at this commit (after merging `claude/sharp-keller-f6iiu2`):**
>
> - **Bundle ID:** `com.vix.pebbleroutines` (Android keeps
>   `com.vix.pebble_routines`). Use it for the App Store Connect record, the
>   RevenueCat iOS app, the Supabase Apple client ID and the Google iOS OAuth
>   client (`IOS_SETUP_CHECKLIST.md`).
> - **Sign in with Apple is offered on iOS** (`sign_in_screen.dart`,
>   `Runner.entitlements`), above Google and Email. It requests the email scope
>   only. The Supabase Apple provider still has to be enabled
>   (`SUPABASE_LIVE_AUDIT.md`, owner task 1).
> - **iPhone only** (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1`), so no iPad screenshots are
>   needed.
> - **iOS builds** come from `codemagic.yaml`, which requires
>   `REVENUECAT_IOS_API_KEY` (`appl_...`) and passes `SENTRY_DSN` when it is
>   set.
> - **Privacy manifest:** `ios/Runner/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` declares no tracking,
>   the collected data types in `APP_PRIVACY_LABELS.md`, and the UserDefaults
>   (`CA92.1`) and file timestamp (`C617.1`) required-reason APIs.
> - **Review risk:** `VISUAL_WALKTHROUGH.md` item 4. The paywall stays on
>   "Loading" when sandbox products don't load, which is a common 2.1
>   rejection. Fix it before you submit.
---

## Keywords (max 100)
Comma separated, no spaces. Apple already indexes the name and subtitle, so
none of these repeat: pebble, routines, checklist, leaving, home, checks,
photos. Plurals are matched automatically, so only one form of each word is
used.
<!-- limit:100 id:ios-keywords keywords exclude:ios-name,ios-subtitle -->
```text
door,lock,straightener,hair,stove,oven,unplug,iron,heater,house,reminder,did,leave,off,bedtime,trip
```
Deliberately left out: "ocd", "anxiety", "worry", "safety", "proof". The
first three would position Pebble as a health product and risk a medical
claims rejection. "Safety" suggests a safety system. "Proof" pulls in
evidence and legal searches.
## Description (max 4000)
The App Store does not index the description for search, so this is written
for people reading it. The Terms of Use and Privacy Policy links are needed
for auto-renewable subscriptions.
<!-- limit:4000 id:ios-description -->
```text
Did I lock the door? Did I unplug the hair straighteners? Is the stove off?
Pebble Routines turns the checks you do before leaving the house into a step-by-step checklist. Go through each step, mark it done, and add a photo when you want something to look back on later. Every completed check is saved with the time you did it.
Pebble is for anyone who has turned back at the front door to check it again, or taken a photo of the straighteners just in case.
HOW IT WORKS
• Create a routine. For example "Leaving the house": straighteners or curling iron unplugged, stove and oven off, windows shut, back door locked, front door locked.
• Run it step by step. One clear screen per step, so the next check is always obvious.
• Add a photo on any step. Take it in the moment, or choose one you already have.
• Look back. Recent history shows what you checked and when.
READY-MADE ROUTINES YOU CAN EDIT
• Everyday departure check: hair tools, stove and oven, toaster, sink, heaters, windows and doors
• Bedtime house check
• Car lock and parking check
• Hotel checkout sweep
• Big trip home shutdown
• School morning run, gym bag, morning pet routine, office switch-off and more
USEFUL EXTRAS
• Reminders: a notification at the time you usually leave
• Voice prompts: record a short note in your own voice for any step (Premium)
• Save a copy to Photos: keep a photo from Pebble in your own library
• Themes, including accessibility themes
PRIVATE BY DEFAULT
• Works without an account. No sign-up needed to start.
• Your routines, history and photos are stored on this device.
• No ads or tracking, and Pebble does not sell your data.
• On the free plan, photos and history are kept for 48 hours, then Pebble deletes its own copies. Pebble never deletes anything from your photo library.
• Cloud backup only starts if you have Premium, sign in, and choose to turn it on.
FREE
• 2 routines, up to 10 steps each
• 1 photo per step
• 48 hours of recent history
• Reminders and ready-made routines
PERSONAL PREMIUM (MONTHLY OR YEARLY)
• Unlimited routines and steps
• Up to 4 photos per step
• 21 days of recent history
• Voice prompts on any step
• Extra themes
• Optional cloud backup and account recovery (needs sign-in and your consent)
• Completion emails: Pebble can email one contact when a routine is done. They accept first, and can stop the emails at any time. Photos and checklist details are not included.
Payment is charged to your Apple Account when you confirm the purchase. Premium renews automatically unless you turn off auto-renew at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. You can manage or cancel it in your App Store account settings. Pebble keeps working on the free plan without Premium.
WHAT PEBBLE IS, AND IS NOT
Pebble is a routine and checklist app. It is not a medical app or treatment, a home security system, or an emergency service, and photos in Pebble are not legal evidence. If checking is taking up a lot of your day, a doctor or other qualified professional can help.
Terms of Use: https://pebbleroutines.com/terms
Privacy Policy: https://pebbleroutines.com/privacy
```
The home-screen widget is Android only, so it is not in the iOS description.

## App Review notes
App Store Connect > App Review Information > Notes. No demo account is needed,
so leave "Sign-in required" unticked.
<!-- limit:4000 id:ios-review-notes -->
```text
Thank you for reviewing Pebble Routines.
WHAT THE APP DOES
Pebble is a local-first checklist app for everyday routines such as "Leaving the house" (straighteners unplugged, stove off, front door locked). Users run a routine step by step, can add a photo to a step, and see recent history with completion times. It is not a medical, safety, or emergency app.
NO ACCOUNT NEEDED
Every core feature works without signing in. Sign-in is optional and is only used for Premium cloud backup, account recovery, and completion emails. Options: Sign in with Apple, Google, or an email one-time code (any email address works).
FREE VS PREMIUM
Free: 2 routines, 10 steps per routine, 1 photo per step, 48 hours of history.
Personal Premium (auto-renewable, monthly or yearly, subscription group "Pebble Premium"): unlimited routines and steps, up to 4 photos per step, 21 days of history, recorded voice prompts, extra themes, and optional cloud backup and completion emails after sign-in.
HOW TO REACH THE SUBSCRIPTION SCREEN
Any of these:
1. Tap "Your account" (top of the home screen), then "Get Premium".
2. Create a third routine. The routine limit opens the Premium screen.
3. In a routine, add a second photo to one step.
4. While editing a step, tap the voice prompt option.
TESTING THE SUBSCRIPTION IN SANDBOX
1. Sign in with a Sandbox Apple Account (Settings > Developer > Sandbox Apple Account, or when prompted at purchase).
2. Open the Premium screen and choose Monthly or Yearly.
3. Confirm the sandbox purchase. Premium unlocks straight away; signing in is not required.
4. To test restore: delete and reinstall the app, open the Premium screen, and tap "Restore purchase".
Purchases are processed by StoreKit through RevenueCat. Cloud backup additionally needs sign-in and the user turning backup on; backup may take a few seconds to confirm the subscription with our server.
SUGGESTED DEMO (2 MINUTES)
1. Open the app. Skip sign-in.
2. Choose the "Everyday departure check" starter routine.
3. Tap Start. Mark the first step done. On a photo step, take or choose a photo (camera and photo permissions are requested only at this moment, with an explanation first).
4. Finish the routine and open History to see the completion time and photo.
5. Optional: open the routine's reminders and set a reminder (notification permission is requested at this moment).
COMPLETION EMAILS (PREMIUM, SIGNED IN)
In a routine's reminders screen, "Notify someone when you finish" lets the user enter one email address. Pebble sends an invitation first; completion emails start only after the recipient accepts. Each email has links to stop the emails or block the sender. Emails contain the routine name, time and step count only.
PERMISSIONS
Camera: proof photos. Photo library: choosing an existing photo and "Save a copy to Photos". Microphone: recording a voice prompt (Premium). Notifications: reminders. No tracking, no ads, no location.
ACCOUNT DELETION
Your account > Delete Account. A web request form is also at https://pebbleroutines.com/delete-account.
Contact: support@pebbleroutines.com
```
Before submitting, check every path in these notes on a TestFlight build.
In particular, confirm the voice prompt entry point and the "Your account"
label are what iOS users see.

### docs/store/LAUNCH_MARKETING_HOOKS.md
# Launch Marketing Hooks: TikTok, Reels and Shorts
Last updated: 4 October 2026
For a solo founder with no budget. Every concept below can be filmed on one
phone in a normal home in under 15 minutes, using Pebble on screen.
## Who this is for, and how to talk to them
Videos of people taking 100 photos of their hair straighteners get
100k-200k likes because viewers recognise themselves. Some of them live with
OCD or checking anxiety, and for some of them it is hard. So:
- **Laugh with, never at.** The joke is "we all do this", never "look how
  weird this person is". Do not stitch or duet someone's video to make fun of
  them.
- **No medical claims, ever.** Do not say Pebble helps, treats, fixes or
  reduces OCD or anxiety. Do not say "break the loop", "stop checking",
  "never worry again", "peace of mind guaranteed", or "you're safe now". Do
  not use #OCD or #anxiety as hashtags to reach people. Pebble is a checklist
  that saves a photo and the time. That is the whole pitch.
- **Don't promise the photo settles it.** For some people, looking at a photo
  again becomes another check. Show Pebble as a record you can look back at,
  not a cure for the doubt.
- **If someone shares that they struggle** in the comments, reply kindly and
  briefly. For example: "That sounds really tiring. If it's taking over your
  day, a GP or doctor can help. Pebble is just a checklist, but I hope it's
  useful." Do not argue or pitch.
- **Film only your own home.** No house numbers, street names, car plates,
  keys up close, or other people's faces. Use a sample routine in the app.
- **Say "photo", not "evidence" or "proof you did it".** "Proof photos" is
  fine only as the feature name.
Posting plan: one video a day for the first two weeks, then three a week.
Reuse the best hook as a reply-to-comment video. Put the store link in your
bio once the app is live, and "Pebble Routines" in on-screen text so people
can search for it.
## 10 video concepts
### 1. "The 100-photo camera roll"
- **Hook (on screen, first 2 seconds):** "My camera roll is 40% hair straighteners"
- **Shots:** scroll a camera roll full of near-identical straightener photos
  (staged on your own phone). Cut to Pebble: run "Leaving the house", take one
  photo on the straighteners step, and the step shows the time.
- **Voiceover or text:** "Now it's one photo, saved with the time, in a list
  that tells me what I've already checked."
- **Caption:** "Anyone else? #hairstraighteners #didileaveiton #leavingthehouse"
### 2. "Turning back at the front door"
- **Hook:** "POV: you're at the bus stop and you can't remember locking the door"
- **Shots:** walking away, stopping, turning round. Freeze-frame. Rewind
  effect to 10 minutes earlier: tapping through "Front door locked" in
  Pebble. Then open History at the bus stop: "Front door locked, 08:02".
- **Caption:** "The 08:02 is the bit I needed. #didilockthedoor"
### 3. "Things I check before I leave, ranked"
- **Hook:** "Ranking the things I check before leaving the house"
- **Shots:** quick tier list with your hand pointing: straighteners, hob or
  stove, back door, windows, iron, heater, the cat. End on the routine built
  in Pebble from exactly that list.
- **Caption:** "What's on yours? I'll add the top answer to the starter list."
  (This invites comments, and you get material for the next video.)
### 4. "Reply to a comment: what's the app?"
- **Hook:** reply to the first comment that asks "what app is this?"
- **Shots:** 20-second screen recording: create a routine, add three steps,
  set "Take a photo" on one, run it.
- **Text:** "Free, no account needed, no ads."
- **Caption:** "Pebble Routines. It's a checklist that saves the time."
### 5. "The straightener step, slow and satisfying"
- **Hook:** "The most satisfying 6 seconds of my morning"
- **Shots:** close-up, with a crisp sound: unplug, coil the cable, put the
  straighteners on the heat mat, phone photo, step goes green in Pebble. Use
  the app's completion sound.
- **Caption:** "Unplugged and photographed by 08:02. #morningroutine #grwm"
### 6. "Builder's tour: solo founder"
- **Hook:** "I built an app because I kept photographing my straighteners"
- **Shots:** you at a desk or kitchen table, phone in hand. Honest 30-second
  story: why you made it, what it does, what it doesn't do ("it's not
  therapy, it's a checklist").
- **Caption:** "Solo dev, no ads, no data selling. Feedback welcome."
  (Founder stories work well with no budget. Be real, show your face if
  you're comfortable.)
### 7. "Holiday edition: the big trip shutdown"
- **Hook:** "The 5am taxi is outside and you're checking the oven for the third time"
- **Shots:** suitcase by the door, run Pebble's "Big trip home shutdown"
  template: fridge, waste out, water, thermostat, plugs. Last step: front
  door.
- **Caption:** "Saving this one for every trip. #travelhack #leavingforholiday"
  (Post before half-term and summer holidays.)
### 8. "Hotel checkout sweep"
- **Hook:** "Every charger I've ever lost is in a hotel room"
- **Shots:** run the "Hotel checkout sweep" template: safe, outlets, under the
  bed, wardrobe, bedside drawer. Photo of the empty safe.
- **Caption:** "Check the safe. Every time. #travelhacks #hotel"
  (This broadens the audience beyond home checks and is lighter in tone.)
### 9. "Wait, did I...? (car edition)"
- **Hook:** "Walking back across the car park to check the car is locked"
- **Shots:** "Car lock and parking check": windows up, no valuables showing,
  lock and listen for the clack, photo of the parking spot. Blur the plate.
- **Caption:** "Bonus: you'll know where you parked. #parkinghack"
### 10. "Bedtime house check, in the dark"
- **Hook:** "Lying in bed wondering if the back door's locked"
- **Shots:** dim lights, Pebble in a dark theme. "Bedtime house check": back
  door, ground-floor windows, stove off, front door. Then into bed and check
  History once: everything listed with times.
- **Caption:** "Done before bed, so it's on the list when I wonder later.
  #nightroutine"
## Hooks to test as text-only posts
Use these over a single still of the app or a stock-style clip of a front
door. Keep the ones that get the most watch time and rewrite them for a full
video.
- "Did I lock the door? (asking for every day of my life)"
- "Straighteners: off. Photo: taken. Time: 08:02."
- "My leaving-the-house checklist, in the order I actually do it"
- "Nobody: ... Me at the front door: one more check"
- "Put the list on your phone, not in your head"
## Free channels besides short video
- **Reddit:** answer genuine "how do you remember if you locked the door"
  threads in r/LifeProTips or r/organization (helpful tips first, mention Pebble only if
  it fits, and follow each subreddit's self-promotion rules). Do not post in
  OCD support communities to promote the app.
- **Pinterest:** pin the "leaving the house checklist" as an image. Pins keep
  getting found for months.
- **Your own story posts:** short build-in-public updates (new template, a
  bug fixed because someone commented).
## Screenshot headline options
Five sets of lead headlines for the first App Store or Play screenshot (the one
that shows in search results). Each is under 40 characters and checked by
`python3 docs/store/check_limits.py`.
<!-- limit:40 id:headline-1 -->
```text
Did I lock the door? Check it here.
```
<!-- limit:40 id:headline-2 -->
```text
Leaving-home checks, step by step
```
<!-- limit:40 id:headline-3 -->
```text
Straighteners off, photo saved at 08:02
```
<!-- limit:40 id:headline-4 -->
```text
Your checks, with the time you did them
```
<!-- limit:40 id:headline-5 -->
```text
One list for the door, stove and plugs
```
Recommended first screenshot: headline 1 (it matches the search phrase and
the short description). Use headline 3 for the photo-step screenshot.
